newsitem.title: DUBAI: Stranded Egyptian pilgrims in Saudi to go home.
newsitem.headline: Stranded Egyptian pilgrims in Saudi to go home.

text.p: Over 1,000 Egyptian pilgrims stranded at Jeddah Islamic Port in Saudi Arabia for the last 10 days will start returning home on Monday, al-Eqtisadiah newspaper said.
The Jeddah-based paper said two scheduled passenger liners, Al-Salam 89 and Al-Salam 95, would begin transporting the pilgrims to Egypt on Monday and Wednesday.
Most of the Egyptians, who performed the minor Umra pilgrimage to Mecca, were stranded because shipping agencies had failed to make proper bookings, diplomats said.
But Egyptian residents in Jeddah said on Monday others had overstayed, taking well-paying illegal jobs as casual labourers or working as beggars.
Witnesses told Reuters some pilgrims had lost their passports and might have to stay until the embassy issued new travel documents.
"Losing their passports eliminates proof of violating (immigration laws)," one said.
Violators of Saudi Arabia's immigration laws are subject to severe penalties including detention, heavy fines and consequent deportation.
Saudi police last week intervened to calm hundreds of enraged Egyptian pilgrims and regular travellers stranded at Jeddah airport because of seat shortages on Egypt Air.
Over 30,000 Egyptians performed the minor pilgrimage to Mecca this year, diplomats said.
